chapter: Kenton, Granz, Parker and the jazz clubs
title: Dating the Kenton recordings
summary: Bauza and the interviewer sort out Kenton's Machito and Peanut Vendor dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay, can we -- can we take it, you know, from an historical point of view? You were involved in the Machito, in the Peanut Vendor of Kenton (phonetic). Incidentally, I checked the dates --

Yeah, and I checked the dates on the Kenton recording from the original books, and "Machito" was recorded about ten months before "Peanut Vendor." So -- but I know you told me once that Kenton was present when you played at Town Hall. Right? There was a concert -- when Kenton played at Town Hall --
No, no, he played Carnegie Hall. I played intermission.
Yeah. Well, I think that's when he named the number after you, because that happened in the beginning of '47, right?
He recorded "Peanut Vendor" -- you got the date?
Yeah, he -- wait a minute. Where did I put it? He recorded --
No, he recorded -- the "Peanut Vendor" was recorded on the 6th of December, 1947.
I think I went back later for another thing.
No, but "Machito" was recorded on the 13th of February, 1947, much earlier.
The "Peanut Vendor" was recorded much earlier --
Later than "Machito." So I think that
